title: Stability interop pilot canvas and testplan
content:
Purpose:
This is a working canvas for a cross-functional reliability pilot ("Interop Pilot") that tests SLO definitions, telemetry plumbing, runbook handoffs, and a canary rollback pattern for model-serving surfaces (hosted API + dedicated). The goal is to run a contained lab (4–6 weeks) with measurable experiments and a reproducible testplan so we can decide whether the proposed SLOs and operational handoffs are fit for scale.

Context and why now:
- Serving runtime introduces variable tail latency with new kernel paths and continuous batching. We need to validate realistic SLOs that reflect both latency-sensitive product routes and batchy background routes.
- Cross-team dependencies: infra for telemetry (prometheus/bigquery), product for route-level SLA context, SRE for oncall/playbooks, and platform-engineering for rollout mechanisms.

High-level objectives (what success looks like):
- SLOs defined for 3 representative route classes and telemetry queries validated end-to-end.
- One end-to-end canary + automated rollback exercise completed (no customer impact).
- Runbook & escalation flows tested with at least one simulated incident (tabletop + live drill).
- Decision: proceed to org-wide SLO adoption, iterate SLO targets, or abandon and rework metrics.

Success criteria (quantitative):
- Observability: latency and success-rate metrics for 95/99/99.9 percentiles available in dashboards within 2 hours of deployment.
- Telemetry accuracy: <2% sampling or aggregation drift between local prometheus scrape and long-term BigQuery aggregates for a 48h window.
- Canary safety: automated rollback triggers on 2/3 of safety signals (latency, error-rate, saturation) and prevents >99.9% of degraded requests from reaching production route.

Hypotheses (to be tested):
H1: Route-level 99th percentile latency target of 250ms for interactive routes is realistic with current kernel selection + batching.
H2: Prefix KV caching reduces p99 latency for repeated conversation tokens by >20% for chat workloads.
H3: Auto-fallback to quantized model variant reduces cost with acceptable quality drop; difference detectable by our eval harness within 48h.

Pilot scope and route taxonomy (representative surfaces):
- interactive-chat: short-turn conversational flows, target latency SLO tightest.
- document-embedding: batch style, SLO focused on throughput and success-rate rather than low p99 latency.
- reranker/summary: medium-latency business logic with higher token counts; monitors sustained CPU/GPU utilization.

Proposed SLOs (draft):
- interactive-chat: 99th percentile latency < 250ms, availability (HTTP 2xx within proxy) >= 99.95% measured per 30d window, error budget 0.05%.
- document-embedding: 95th percentile latency < 2s, success_rate >= 99.9% per 30d window.
- reranker: 99th percentile latency < 700ms, GPU-saturation incidents <= 2/month.

Measurement plan / telemetry queries (placeholders):
- PromQL (latency p99): histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))
- Success rate (BQ): SELECT route, SUM(CASE WHEN status_code LIKE '2__' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(1) FROM `prod.request_logs` WHERE _PARTITIONTIME BETWEEN ... GROUP BY route
- KV cache hit ratio: rate(cache_hits[5m]) / rate(cache_requests[5m])  -- alert if < 0.6 for 10m

Experiment matrix (each experiment has owner, measurement, rollback condition):
1) Latency regression probe (A/B canary)
   - Owner: Owen Park
   - What: Deploy kernel optimization on 10% traffic for interactive-chat for 3 days.
   - Measure: p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, CPU/GPU utilization, token throughput.
   - Rollback: if p99 increases >10% and error_rate > 0.2% absolute.
2) Prefix cache effectiveness (feature flag flip)
   - Owner: Priya Nair
   - What: Enable prefix/KV caching for a slice of sessions; track hit rate and latency per-session.
   - Measure: median latency per session, p99 for repeated tokens.
   - Rollback: if cache misses exceed 40% or quality regressions observed in eval harness.
3) Quantized fallback (tiered routing)
   - Owner: Diego Martinez
   - What: Route low-priority traffic to a quantized variant when utilization > 70% on a node pool.
   - Measure: cost per token, quality delta vs baseline measured by automated evals.
   - Rollback: if eval quality delta exceeds threshold (configurable per workload).

Runbook and escalation (short sketch):
- Primary oncall: SRE-serving (rotation).
- Triage first 15m: owner identifies whether metric breach is telemetry, model, infra, or client.
- If availability breach persists >30m or user-impacting errors visible, escalate to product-incident lead + platform-eng.
- Automated playbook: run preconfigured remediation steps (scale pool, fallback route), then create an incident and run tabletop.

Canary + rollout plan (technical flow):
- Stage commit -> internal canary on staging infra -> 10% production shadow for 24h -> 30% for 6h -> 60% for 1h -> 100% if green.
- Monitoring check gates at each step: p99, error_rate, queue_length, cache_hit_ratio.
- Automated rollback at each gate via orchestration script if any gate fails.

Cross-functional commitments (who does what):
- Serving runtime: implement metrics hooks, kernel flags, rollout orchestration (Owen, Jinwoo).
- SRE: define alerts, own oncall triage, runbook (Marta).
- Observability/Platform: dashboards, BI queries, retention for long-term analysis (Priya).
- Product/PM: clarify customer critical routes and acceptable SLO tradeoffs (Samira).
- Solutions Eng / Customer Success: validate real-customer workflows where applicable (Diego).

Sprint schedule (6-week lab):
Week 0 (prep): wire telemetry, create dashboards, create sandbox canary job. Owners: Observability + Serving.
Week 1: baseline measurement (collect 7d baseline), finalize SLO thresholds.
Week 2: run prefix cache experiment (feature-flagged small cohort).
Week 3: kernel canary (10% traffic) + monitor.
Week 4: quantized-fallback pilot and eval harness run.
Week 5: runbook drill (simulated incident), tabletop with oncall.
Week 6: retro, decision meeting, proposals for next-phase org rollout.

Key risks and mitigations:
- Telemetry gaps: run parallel sampling to BigQuery to detect drift; keep a small retention to re-run slices.
- Customer impact from canary: use synthetic traffic + low-customer-percent slices; ensure auto-rollbacks are tested before canary.
- False positives in alerts: tune thresholds using baseline window and run a 48h quiet period before enabling automatic escalations.

Open decisions we need to resolve in the first week:
- Final numeric SLO thresholds per route class (tentative values above).
- Exact telemetry retention / aggregation window in BigQuery for SLO computation.
- What constitutes a quality regression for quantized fallback (metric + evaluation harness threshold).

Quick links & tickets (working list):
- Confluence draft: SR interop pilot page (linked above)
- Jira epic: ENGSR-4123 (pilot epic)
- Dashboards: link (TBD) but owners: Priya for query templates
- PR: serving-runtime PR #987 implementing kernel flags

Immediate next steps (this doc owner):
1) Schedule kickoff with SRE + Observability + Platform (target: within 48h).
2) Create baseline data export job to BigQuery and confirm sample parity (owner: Priya).
3) Wire up canary orchestration script and test rollback in staging (owner: Owen).
4) Prepare evaluation harness set and baseline examples for quantized fallback (owner: Diego).

Notes to self / scratch ideas:
- Consider adding synthetic traffic that mimics multi-turn distribution rather than uniform.
- Might expose an internal "slo-bench" lab that other teams can reuse for smaller pilots.
- Track cost delta separately so decision to adopt quantized fallback can be economic as well as quality-driven.

Attach: short checklist for kickoff (copy into Jira):
- [ ] Invite: SRE-serving, Observability, Platform-eng, Product PM, Solutions Eng
- [ ] Baseline export to BigQuery validated
- [ ] Dashboards created (p50/p95/p99, success_rate, cache_hit_ratio)
- [ ] Canary orchestration smoke test passed in staging
- [ ] Runbook draft uploaded to Confluence

End of canvas.

-- Samira (owner)
